Zygophyllaceae.key_door: compound leaves/stipules + floral nectar glands + lobed/multi-locular ovary → segmented fruit

Krameriaceae.key_door: hemiparasitic hairy plant + petaloid sepals + 2 oil petals + poricidal anthers + one-seeded barbed fruit

lineage_lesson: Sister families share dryland history but diverge strongly: Zygophyllaceae retains mostly radial conventional flowers and multipart fruits, while Krameriaceae specializes in oil-bee pollination and hemiparasitism.
guardrails: Do not use compound leaves alone to call Zygophyllaceae.
Do not disturb Krameria roots merely to prove hemiparasitism.
